statement: The first line holds n and k; the second holds n integers, negatives allowed. Print how many contiguous subarrays sum to exactly k. Carry the running prefix sum and a map from prefix value to how many times it has occurred, seeded with 0 mapping to 1 for the empty prefix. At each element, add the stored count of prefix minus k - every one of those earlier markers starts a subarray ending here with sum k - then record the current prefix. Counts, not indexes: this problem tallies, the longest-variants measure.
constraints: -10000 ≤ values ≤ 10000; the count fits in 64 bits.

example.why: Prefixes 1, 2, 3: prefix 2 closes against the seed, prefix 3 against the earlier 1.

hint: Lookup before insert - the current prefix must never pair with itself.
mistake: Skipping the seed; every subarray that starts at index 0 silently goes uncounted.
